subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Threatened, Inevitable, Incomplete, Missed and Septic Abortion

steps.tx: Bleeding in early pregnancy with a closed cervix and living fetus is **threatened abortion**. Most such pregnancies continue normally after the bleeding settles. Ultrasound confirming cardiac activity guides reassurance and follow up. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Threatened abortion bleeds with a closed cervix and most pregnancies continue normally.

steps.tx: An abortion that cannot be stopped because the cervix has opened is **inevitable abortion**. Membranes may bulge through the cervix on examination. Management supports completion with evacuation when needed. Correlating this finding with imaging and laboratory results prevents both delayed treatment and unnecessary intervention in most patients.
steps.say: Inevitable abortion cannot be stopped once the cervix has opened.

steps.tx: Partial passage of products leaving tissue inside the uterus is **incomplete abortion**. Bleeding can be heavy because retained tissue prevents uterine contraction. Evacuation by suction or medical method completes the process. Early recognition matters because timely treatment gives clearly better outcomes than waiting for complications to develop first.
steps.say: Incomplete abortion retains tissue that prevents contraction and causes heavy bleeding.

steps.tx: Fetal death without expulsion, often found on routine scan, is **missed abortion**. The uterus fails to grow and pregnancy symptoms fade. Expectant, medical and surgical options are all offered by gestation and preference. Students should connect this fact with the presenting symptoms, since examination questions usually test that clinical link directly.
steps.say: Missed abortion is fetal death without expulsion, found on routine scanning.

steps.tx: Infected retained products causing fever, pain and offensive discharge define **septic abortion**. It follows unsafe abortion practices and can progress to septic shock. Resuscitation, antibiotics and urgent evacuation save lives. Documenting this finding clearly in the notes guides the next clinician and supports safe, well planned further management.
steps.say: Septic abortion infects retained products and can progress to septic shock.

steps.tx: Medical abortion using mifepristone followed by misoprostol is standard to nine weeks and beyond in many protocols, termed **medical termination**. Success exceeds ninety five percent in early gestation. Surgical backup covers the small failure group. When this picture is seen in practice, urgent senior review is wise whenever there is any doubt about severity.
steps.say: Medical termination with mifepristone and misoprostol succeeds in over ninety five percent early.

steps.tx: Rh negative women need anti-D after abortion to prevent **isoimmunisation**. Even early sensitisation can affect future pregnancies. Guidelines vary by gestation and method, so local protocol is followed. Understanding this mechanism explains the symptoms, the investigation findings and the logic behind each step of treatment given.
steps.say: Anti-D after abortion prevents isoimmunisation in Rh negative women.

steps.tx: Complete passage of all products with settling bleeding is **complete abortion**. Ultrasound showing an empty uterus confirms it. No evacuation is needed and routine follow up suffices. This distinction changes management, so it should be settled early rather than after empirical treatment has already begun.
steps.say: Complete abortion passes everything with settling bleeding and needs no evacuation.

steps.tx: Bleeding after twelve weeks with pain suggests placental causes rather than abortion, a matter of **differential diagnosis**. Cervical causes, ectopic pregnancy and molar disease also present with early bleeding. Ultrasound location and viability sort most cases quickly. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Early bleeding differentials include ectopic and molar disease, sorted quickly by ultrasound.
